data.body:
Landed and verified from merged main.

Changes: 1028 (deadlock fix), 1039 (JSON field assertions), 1040 (rename to doctor) — all MERGED; 1040 is f4a3063df966. The stack was rebased onto 1044 (another ticket fix for the DET short-circuit / reuse-test interaction) so CI tested the real combination rather than each half in isolation.

Verified against merged main:
- `rebar doctor --output json` -> 8 findings, keys {finding_count, findings, pre_repair_tag_oid}
- `rebar link-audit` -> "Error: unknown subcommand" (verb removed)
- `rebar help` lists: doctor      Diagnose the store and heal what is safe to fix (--repair)

Final AC disposition for the scheduling-affecting criterion: 8 findings remain, all mis-escalated, and for every one the BLOCKED side (source for depends_on, target for blocks) is closed. Closed tickets never appear in ready/next-batch, so 0 of 8 can affect scheduling. Each is blocked from repair by add_dependency correctly refusing a link whose source is closed.

Cumulative remediation under this ticket: 18 bad edges found on this repository tracker, 12 repaired (all 9 ancestor-blocking + 3 mis-escalated), 8 inert residuals.

Scope change recorded at operator direction: a standalone link-audit verb was rejected for core, so the command became the first check of `doctor` and is now referenced from both doctor epics (dabb-7d4b-f5bc-40e6 and 18ae-4f54-a85b-4ddb), which are linked relates_to for a later brainstorm merge. The re-parenting drift found here — two NEW mis-escalated edges with OPEN endpoints appeared within hours of remediation — is recorded on those epics as in-scope follow-up: re-parent should auto-remediate or be denied, with doctor as the backstop rather than the primary defence.
